name: Wyn
note: The guide (Michael, 2026-10-16, #90, #91): a neighbour from the farm lane who came to your yard when the bell stopped and has not gone home. Warm, slightly cheeky, welcoming. Every topic is a system as built, checked against the code and the Controls screen; a new system adds its question here in the same commit.

lines: They are close. Is your door shut?
I would be indoors, if I were you.
Dark out. A fire and a shut door help.
Made it to morning, then. Well done.
Ask me anything, if you are stuck.
Not sure where to start? I might.
Lovely day for it. Whatever it is.
Quick words, then, the dead are close.
What do you want to know?
Up late? Same. Ask me what you like.
Oh, hello. You look like you could use a hand.
I know this valley. Ask what you like.

options.text: How do I keep them out?
What is Tab, C, and the belt?
Can I water a field faster?

say: Wyn. I live down the farm lane, or I did.
I keep a few hens. Well. I kept a few hens.
The bell stopped on the third day, and I came up the lane.
Your yard had a gate and a well. It seemed polite to stay.
The dead do not seem to mind me. I do not ask why.
It began quietly. Then the bell stopped, and they were in the street.
The ones who are left stay indoors. Some of us stay in and wait.
Wells, and any water you can stand beside: the river, the ponds, the trough.
Fill a waterskin there. Drink from it, or let it sip for you when you get thirsty.
It is all fine to drink. Nobody has been poorly from it yet.
Bread, cheese, apples, anything in a chest or a barrel.
A food on your belt eats with its key. Food mends you hungry or full, and a full belly mends faster on its own.
Cooked food fills more than raw. Any lit fire that cooks will do, and the oven bakes.
A fire burns its fuel down over the hours and goes out. Logs feed a hearth, a campfire, or the oven; the forge wants charcoal.
A station with a fire only works while it is lit, and waits for you if it goes out.
T lights the torch in your hand. A tinderbox does the lighting.
A bed, indoors. Time runs fast until morning, and nobody wakes you.
With friends in the world, it runs fast only when everyone is in bed.
If the dead have been hunting you indoors, you will not get to sleep until they leave.

options.text: How do I keep them out?

say: Doors and shutters open and close on E. Closed shutters block sight.
B boards up the nearest opening, and holding it pulls a board off.
Windows have shutters, not glass. Nobody climbs through one, but they do batter shutters and boards, and then go round to a door.
A sealed room is safe. It is also a cell, so mind your water and food.
Left-click swings what you hold; with nothing, fists. Hold it to draw a bow.
Hold right-click for the off hand's stance, a shield's block, say. Q or middle-click is the main hand's other mode.
Space shoves the dead back, no damage. Every weapon wears out by the dead it puts down, and nothing mends it.
Stations: the workbench at the joiner's, the forge and anvil at the smithy, the oven at the baker's, the loom at the weaver's.
Open one with E. It works from your bag and from every container beside it.
Planks and sticks first. Iron takes a forge.
Bites bleed, and bleeding drains health. A bandage stops it at once.
Health comes back slowly while you are fed and watered, and about four times as fast asleep.
Food heals a bit as well. It is a stopgap, not a cure.
Tab opens your bag, a grid where things take the room they take.
C is your character: what you wear and hold. Double-click equips or unequips.

Your rope belt has three slots: 1 the main hand, 2 the off hand, 3 utility. A hand slot's key draws what is there into that hand, or eats the food on it; the utility slot's key only eats, and anything else rides there spare. A waterskin on it sips by itself. A leather belt adds 4 and 5, a second main and off hand.
N opens the build menu: walls, doors, windows. X shows what you can remove. A door or a window, boarding up, and X all want a smith's hammer on you; a log wall wants a hatchet.
R turns what you are placing. Furniture can be carried on your head and set down.
Walls hold. A door, a board, or a fence, they can batter down.

options.text: How do I keep them out?

say: A hoe in a hand turns bare grass or dirt to soil. Seed goes in soil, and water keeps it growing.
Watered soil stays wet for two days. A dry crop only pauses. It never dies.
Harvest when it is ripe, with the tool for it carried: a shovel for potatoes and garlic, a dirk for cabbage and pumpkin, a scythe for rye. A few seeds come back and the soil stays.
A scythe takes the ripe rye on the three tiles ahead at a swing.
The granaries at Hollow Farm and the mill keep seed of every crop.
A pickaxe in your hand mines a rock for stone and an ore rock for iron ore. The ore rocks come back after a few days.
A forge smelts two ore to a bar, and the forge wants charcoal. A clamp makes that from logs, slowly.
Bars and a stick, a hammer in hand, make tools at the anvil.
A bucket in your bag, on your belt, or in a hand fills at any water and pours over a three by three of crops.
One pour a fill, and a wall stops the water. It is only for fields: you cannot drink from it.
Flax grows like any crop. The loom turns two flax into linen cloth, and cloth into bandages, a cap, breeches, or a tunic.
A dirk on you tears an old garment into rags at a workbench, and a rag will do where a recipe wants cloth.
The weaver's chest has flax seed and a dirk in it, if nobody has been.
Grain goes to the millstones at the mill, by Long Acre. Two grain grind to one flour, and no fire is needed.
Flour bakes into bread at an oven. A pumpkin makes a pie there too.
Seed for every crop is in the granaries, at Hollow Farm and beside the mill.
A rod in your hand, a cast at water beside you, and then you wait.
What bites depends on the water: the river and the ponds each have their own.
Anything you catch cooks at a lit fire.
W A S D walk, Shift sprints, Z or the wheel zooms. E does the nearest thing.
Right-click shows everything you can do to what is under the cursor. Esc closes what is open, else pauses.
The Controls screen has the rest, if you want them in one place.

options.text: What is Tab, C, and the belt?

say: M opens it. It fills in as you look: anything anyone in the valley has seen, yours or a friend's, and it keeps it.
North is up and to the right, whichever way you are facing. Your marker is gold; a friend's is white.
It shows where people are and never the dead. A clear map is not a clear road.
